quotes.text: The key failure isn't inattentive employees. It's the outdated system that assumes learning can succeed when stripped away from context.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes training failure as a system problem instead of a people problem.

quotes.text: This is what people mean when they talk about learning in the flow of work. It's the idea that the act of learning is not a break from work, but a natural part of it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise definition of learning in the flow of work.

quotes.text: Embedded guidance, however, updates with the product itself. When a new button appears or a feature moves, the help system adjusts immediately.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why in-product help keeps pace with evergreen updates while static training does not.

quotes.text: Sticking with static training is like buying a printed road map while everyone else is using Google Maps.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable metaphor for outdated training methods.

takeaways: Classroom workshops fail because knowledge learned out of context fades quickly along the forgetting curve.
Microsoft 365 already embeds learning through Microsoft Search, in-product tips and Viva Learning inside Teams.
Because embedded guidance updates with the product, it keeps employees current with evergreen changes that static training cannot match.
hook: Employees forget most of what they learn in Microsoft 365 workshops within days, and help desks pay the price. This episode shows IT and adoption leads how in-product guidance, Microsoft Search and Viva Learning deliver micro lessons right in the flow of work. Learn where to redirect training budgets so skills actually stick.
